core.title: Bind every implementation file to at least one acceptance
core.given: Any implementation (non-test) source file — new, modified, or untouched
core.when: It exists in the repository (continuous obligation, not only when the header is edited)
core.then: The file's header MUST contain an acceptance-binding block (the stack's binding syntax, profile: urn.binding.acceptance) with at least one entry, each entry naming a real, exactly-declared acceptance URN that exercises the file; an empty binding block counts as absent.
prefer: During GREEN, derive the binding from the acceptance being implemented.
Keep existing valid bindings; add only the acceptance that genuinely covers this file.
Use the exact declared acceptance URN.
One entry suffices; more are encouraged when they genuinely cover the file.
Pick the acceptance whose scenario drives code in this file (check its behavior, not just its name).
Prove the binding by running the behavioral acceptance named in the file's acceptance-binding header and confirming it passes.
avoid: Adding unrelated tests merely to make the block non-empty.
Claiming coverage from an acceptance that does not exercise the implementation.
Leaving a bare binding line with no entries beneath it.
unless: The file is a test file — the other end of this binding.
core.why: The file's URN says what the file IS; the acceptance binding says what PROVES it, closing the acceptance-to-implementation loop that stack migrations silently break. An empty binding block (half-finished backfill) would report full coverage with zero bindings.
evidence: The behavioral acceptance named in the file's acceptance-binding header passes.

The file's binding block names the acceptance that actually proves it, and every listed entry is a real, exactly-declared acceptance that exercises the file (judged by inspecting the acceptance's behavior against the declared acceptances; not syntactically observable).
The stack's traceability check reports no missing-or-empty acceptance-binding finding for the file.
verification: Per-file check of the binding block (profile: urn.binding.acceptance): the binding line must be present AND followed by at least one entry naming an acceptance URN; the check covers presence and non-emptiness of the block only.

An empty binding block (a binding line with no entries) is treated as absent and reported identically to a missing block: it is the shape a half-finished backfill leaves and would otherwise report full coverage with zero bindings.
Threshold: one entry satisfies the rule; more are encouraged.
Test files are excluded from detection (the implementation/test classification comes from the profile, roles.assignment).

Entry resolution against plan artifacts (profile: roots.plan) is out of scope for this per-file check; a silent check therefore does not prove that the listed entries are real, exactly declared, or exercise the file.
Disposition strict, severity 2: the stack's ATDD tooling fails on every finding of this rule; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: acceptance-binding block missing or empty in an implementation file

fires: A new implementation file is written without an acceptance-binding block in its header.
An existing, untouched implementation file has no acceptance-binding block in its header.
An implementation file's header carries a binding block with no entries beneath it (the shape of a half-finished backfill).
Files are migrated or rewritten onto a new stack and the new files lack headers.
An implementation file's binding block is populated but names an invented acceptance URN, or an acceptance that does not exercise the file (the check may stay silent; the rule still applies).
An implementation file's binding block mixes at least one valid binding with one or more invented, not-exactly-declared, or non-exercising entries (the valid entry does not excuse the invalid ones).
The stack's traceability check reports a missing-or-empty acceptance-binding finding for the file.
doesNotFire: The file is a test file (unit, acceptance, or e2e test) — it is the other end of the binding.

profileRequirements.meaning: The header syntax by which an implementation file binds itself to the acceptance(s) that prove it, and what an empty binding block looks like.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a `Tested-By:` line followed by one or more `- test:` entry lines (each naming an acceptance URN); a `Tested-By:` line with no entries is an empty block

profileRequirements.meaning: How the stack decides that a file is an implementation (non-test) source file — in scope for this rule — versus a test file (unit/acceptance/e2e), which is out of scope.
profileRequirements.bunValue: implementation = every non-test source file in the repository, new, modified, or pre-existing and untouched; test files are excluded (the other end of the binding)

profileRequirements.meaning: Where plan artifacts live; entry resolution against them is explicitly out of scope for this rule's per-file check.

bunOnly.reason: Finding ids belong to this stack's detector; each realization reports its own ids for the same neutral finding (acceptance-binding block missing or empty).

bunOnly.text: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-HEADER-003 / BUN-GREEN-HEADER-TESTED-BY-001 finding for the file.
bunOnly.reason: Names this realization's validator and finding ids; the core keeps the generic 'no missing-or-empty binding finding from the stack's traceability check'.

bunOnly.text: Realized by validator bun_green_traceability_detector (stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector); core alias GREEN-HEADER-003, stack alias BUN-GREEN-HEADER-TESTED-BY-001.
bunOnly.reason: Detector, validator and alias ids identify this one realization; the core describes the check generically and carries only the severity/disposition in core:verification.

neutralityNotes: The concrete binding syntax (`Tested-By:` line plus `- test:` entries) is carried by urn.binding.acceptance and by bun.json itself as the reference example; the core names only 'the acceptance-binding block'. bun.json does not state the acceptance URN shape, so urn.acceptance and urn.declaration are not listed as profileRequirements; the 'real, exactly-declared' requirement stays a behavioral judgment (evidence) that this rule's check explicitly does not perform. roles.assignment is bun.json's own negative definition (non-test source file), not a concrete mechanism. Detector/validator/finding ids (bun_green_traceability_detector, GREEN-HEADER-003, BUN-GREEN-HEADER-TESTED-BY-001) are bunOnly; the core describes the check generically. The word 'stack migration' in fires/why is kept: it is neutral across stacks by design.
